title: Clauses
examples: What is the difference between a main clause and a subordinate clause?
Can you give me an example of a relative clause?
How do I know when to use commas with these clauses?

explain.say: Today we are learning about clauses which are groups of words.

draw.text: Clauses: Groups of words with verbs

explain.say: A main clause can stand alone as a complete sentence.
A subordinate clause cannot stand alone as a complete sentence.
Relative clauses are a type of subordinate clause that gives extra information.

draw.text: Relative Clauses: Extra info about a noun

explain.say: For example, the girl who won the race cheered loudly.

draw.text: The girl who won the race

explain.say: In everyday life, think about directions you follow.

faq.q: How do I know if a clause is main or subordinate?
faq.a: If you can say it out loud by itself and it makes sense, it is a main clause. If it leaves you hanging, it is subordinate.
asks: Can I use this clause alone?
Does it need another clause to make sense?

faq.q: What words usually start a subordinate clause?
faq.a: Common words include because, although, when, if, and since. These words signal that the clause depends on another idea.

faq.q: What is the difference between a relative clause and a subordinate clause?
faq.a: All relative clauses are subordinate, but not all subordinate clauses are relative clauses. Relative clauses specifically describe a noun.
asks: What is the job of a relative clause?

faq.q: Do I always need commas with relative clauses?
faq.a: Sometimes you do. If the clause gives essential information, you usually do not use commas. If it gives extra detail, you often need commas.

faq.q: What is the role of 'who' in a relative clause?
faq.a: The word who is used to refer to people. For example, 'The student who studied passed.'
asks: Which word do I use for people?

facts: A clause must contain at least one subject and one verb.
Main clauses can stand alone as a complete thought.
Subordinate clauses begin with a subordinating conjunction like 'because' or 'when'.
Relative clauses use words like 'who' or 'which' to add detail.

quiz.say: The book which is on the top shelf belongs to me.
quiz.show: The book which is on the top shelf

options.show: The book which is on the top shelf
options.say: The book which is on the top shelf

options.show: which is on the top shelf belongs to me
options.say: which is on the top shelf belongs to me

quiz.why: The clause 'which is on the top shelf' describes the noun 'book' and cannot stand alone.

wrong.1: This is only the subject, not the whole dependent clause.
wrong.2: This is missing the main subject it describes.
wrong.3: This is a main verb phrase, but it lacks a clear subject.

quiz.say: My friend who lives nearby is very kind.
quiz.why: This clause describes 'friend' and starts with the relative pronoun 'who'.

wrong.0: This is a noun phrase, but it is not the specific subordinate clause requested.
wrong.2: This is the noun phrase, not the clause that describes it.
wrong.3: This is the main verb phrase that completes the thought.
